lines.text: Do you know why people are using Orbi Transfer?
Monday morning. A small studio, one big client, and a deadline at five.
Usually the files are scattered across a dozen chats, and nobody knows who's doing what.
So you open a Space. One private room, with its own name and a passcode.
Everyone types the passcode once, picks a name, and they're in. No accounts. No email invites.
From now on, files sent here only reach your team. The rest of the office sees nothing.
Then you add a task. New logo for the client. For Maya.
You set its route: in progress, in review, approved, delivered. Every step is a light.
Maya sends her drafts and wires them to the task, so the files hang right off the job they belong to.
As the work moves, the light moves. Orange, then blue, then green. Everyone sees it change, live.
And every move is written down. Who did it, and when.
Client changed their mind? One step turns it red. Cancelled. No confusion.
And every file is still locked on the sender's phone. Only members can open it.
Files burn after thirty minutes, tasks after up to eight hours with Pro. A clean board, every day.
Orbi Transfer dot com. Try it with your team tomorrow.
